hints: Notice the given $9.0 \, \text{V}$, $5.6 \, \text{k}\Omega = 5600 \, \Omega$ and time of one minute $= 60 \, \text{s}$.
Connect current to charge flow using $I = V/R$ and then $Q = I t$, where $Q$ is the total charge passing the point.
Connect total charge to electron number using $Q = n e$ with $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$, then evaluate $n = Q/e$.
walkthrough: Use Ohm's law to find the current: $I = V/R = 9.0/5600 \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{A}$.
Find the charge passing in one minute: $Q = I t \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 \approx 9.64 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{C}$.
Use quantisation of charge $Q = n e$ with $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$: $n = Q/e$.

options.A: Too large by a factor of 1000, from using $5.6 \, \Omega$ instead of $5.6 \, \text{k}\Omega = 5600 \, \Omega$ for the resistance.
options.B: Too large by about a factor of 17, from an error in combining current, 60 s time and electron charge $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$.
options.C: Current $I = V/R$ gives about $1.61 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{A}$, charge in 60 s is about $0.096 \, \text{C}$, giving $Q/e \approx 6.0 \times 10^{17}$ electrons.
options.D: Too small by a factor of 60, from using $t = 1 \, \text{s}$ instead of $t = 60 \, \text{s}$ for one minute.
